page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfg6.10xlarge is a general-purpose, compute-capable virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 40 dedicated physical cores and 40 vCPUs using the x86_64 architecture, running on an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor clocked at 3.1 GHz. The instance is equipped with 192.0 GB of RAM, providing a resource density of 4.8 GB per core. It does not include local storage or GPU hardware, relying instead on network-attached storage and featuring a baseline network bandwidth of 12 Gbps.

Benchmark results place the ecs.hfg6.10xlarge in the average performance category across multiple workloads. The Intel Xeon processor achieves a stress-ng single-core score of 1438.99 and a multi-core score of 38378.07, supported by a PassMark CPU score of 34691.95. Memory performance is characterized by a read-only small block cached bandwidth of 2133.36 GB/sec, which drops to 108.89 GB/sec for uncached large blocks, and a write bandwidth of 48.09 GB/sec. In application-specific tests, the instance demonstrates a static web serving throughput of 25.35 GB/sec and processes 34.78 million Redis SET operations per second. For lightweight machine learning tasks, it handles 135M model LLM text generation at 76.66 tokens/second and 7B model generation at 12.71 tokens/second.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the dedicated core allocation and high base clock speed of 3.1 GHz offer predictable performance for compute-intensive tasks without the overhead of hyperthreading. However, the lack of bundled local storage requires external block storage, which should be factored into the overall infrastructure architecture. This instance is well-suited for workloads such as database operations, software compilation, web serving, and multi-threaded data decompression.
